text: Koko-Bera is widely spoken by Kokoberrin Y223 people at Kowanyama and Normanton. In modern times, Koko-Bera speakers also use Kurtjar G33 (Black, c2007:1). See also Koko Babangk Y203.

text: Guide and Scout groups perform the song across the United States, Canada, New Zealand, and the United Kingdom, where it has been part of the traditional campfire repertoire for decades. For many people outside Australia, it is the first Australian song they ever learn – and often the only one they know by heart. The round structure is a large part of why it travels so well. No sheet music is strictly required.
